tagline: Out of Pittsboro to a ring where nothing grows, they say.
intro: NC 902 leaves the Chatham County Courthouse in Pittsboro and heads out into the lower Piedmont, past Round Top Mountain and over the Rocky River, through farmland and forest to Harpers Crossroads. From there it runs on to NC 42, and Howard Mill Road finishes the trip through the Moore County countryside to NC 705.

The road takes its name from a bare ring in the woods near Bear Creek. The story goes that the devil walks it in circles at night, plotting new trouble for the world, and that nothing has grown in it for a hundred years.

moments.title: Pittsboro
moments.text: The county seat is named for William Pitt the Younger, though the county is named for his father, and the town was once considered for both the state university and the capital.

moments.title: Devil's Tramping Ground
moments.text: From Harpers Crossroads a side road leads 1.7 miles to a gravel pull-off, and a path runs a few hundred feet into the woods to the bare circle.

practical: The Devil's Tramping Ground is on private property.
